A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FARTrack study. Their text, equations, Tables 1-12, Figures 1-8, and Appendices A-G are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original FARTrack benchmark results, component ablations, attention visualizations, and training-cost comparisons in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark measurements and supplementary experiments, including the template, distillation, and training-cost analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2-3.5 retain the same multi-template architecture, task-specific self-distillation, inter-frame sparsification, training losses, and autoregressive inference. The revised experimental prose describes the existing procedure.

E1.justification: COCO2017 pretraining and evaluation on GOT-10k, TrackingNet, LaSOT, LaSOText, NFS, UAV123, and VastTrack remain unchanged. No training domain, evaluation task, or supplementary test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged throughout the benchmark and ablation comparisons, including the appendix scratch-trained models. SMAT's citation changes from Gopal and Amer (2024b) to (2024) after reference deduplication; the evaluated method is unchanged.

E3.justification: Model configurations, input sizes, training budgets, benchmark protocols, metrics, and speed-testing hardware are unchanged in Section 4.1, Table 2, and Appendix A. The rewritten Table 9 discussion retains the same six-layer models and matched training settings.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same distillation, sparsification, retention-ratio, attention-sampling, component, and visualization analyses. Appendices B-F preserve the template-count/update, attention, scratch-training, and training-cost comparisons without additional evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these experiments.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted curves, and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains FARTracktiny's 70.6% GOT-10k AO and FARTrackpico's 343 GPU FPS and 121 CPU FPS. Appendix results and training-time measurements are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (1), the loss definitions, and mathematical descriptions remain unchanged. Neither version contains added or revised formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning temporal information preservation, sequence-level sparsification, and the speed-performance balance. Added citations and wording edits do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The shortened Section 4.3 prose preserves the explanations based on semantic mismatch and representational capacity. Interpretations of excessive pruning, template-update failures, and the accuracy tradeoff against top-performing trackers remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract's code hyperlink changes from wangguijiepedeval/FARTrack.git to MIV-XJTU/FARTrack.git, and v2 displays the full address. This revises access information; repository availability or contents cannot be established from the PDFs. Implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, and training-time disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction adds four references: Yang et al. (2026), Zeng et al. (2025a, 2025b), and Qi et al. (2026), supporting the practical deployment motivation. The substantive related-work discussion and FARTrack's novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 tightens several Section 4.3 paragraphs, makes a small grammatical correction in the conclusion, updates affiliations, and adds acknowledgments. It also relocates the LaSOT discussion and consolidates the duplicated Gopal and Amer reference. The overall organization and appendix text are retained.

P2.justification: The author and affiliation block is reformatted, and prose and references reflow around the existing displays. Figures 1-8 are visually identical; tables retain their structure and results. The appendices shift by one page without changes to their body layout.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves readability and documentation through tighter Section 4.3 prose, removal of a duplicated reference, funding acknowledgment, and an explicitly displayed code address. The PDFs do not establish improved repository availability. Methods, evidence, scientific interpretations, and appendices remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited to presentation and documentation.
